CHIEF COMPLAINT
Acne on the face

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Kayla Ward is a 18-year-old female presenting with acne located on the face that started approximately two years ago and is present most every day. Patient reports that acne is worse on the forehead, central cheeks, and chin, with minimal involvement of the chest and back. She denies associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain. Patient notes that acne may worsen with sweating from sports activities in the fall. Denies correlation with menstrual cycle. Patient has been using over-the-counter treatments including Persa-Gel and regular facial washing, which she reports are somewhat helpful. Current skincare routine includes washing face with water and washcloth in the morning, and using ELF Super Clarity Cleanser, toner, and Persa-Gel at night. Today is reported as a relatively good day for acne. Mother notes that acne flares were most significant when patient started school sports in the fall due to sweating, despite good adherence to facial care regimen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies itching, bleeding, or pain associated with acne. Regular menstrual periods for approximately two years.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
None reported

MEDICATIONS
ELF Super Clarity Cleanser (topical)
Persa-Gel (topical)
Toner (topical)
Sunscreen SPF 30 (seasonal use)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not reported

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with parents and sister. Household pets include one dog, one bird, and bunnies. Currently in 7th grade. Participates in basketball, volleyball, and tap dance. Wears sunscreen SPF 30 in the summer months.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-appearing female
Skin: Multiple benign nevi on trunk and extremities. Scattered skin-colored papules. Open and closed comedones. Erythematous papules on face, primarily on forehead with additional involvement of central cheeks and chin. Chest and back relatively spared. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
Clinical diagnosis: Mild to moderate acne, predominantly comedonal with small inflammatory component

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Mild to moderate facial acne, primarily comedonal with inflammatory component. Plan: Initiate topical therapy. Morning routine: wash face with mild cleanser, apply noncomedogenic moisturizer with sunscreen SPF 30 or higher. Evening routine: wash face with mild cleanser, allow to dry, apply adapalene 0.1% cream in thin layer to affected areas starting a few nights per week and gradually increasing to nightly use; follow with Persa-Gel in thin layer to affected areas, then noncomedogenic moisturizer. Counsel patient regarding sun protection and potential side effects of adapalene including dryness and irritation. Multiple benign nevi noted on trunk and extremities with no worrisome features; no intervention needed at this time. Follow-up visit in six months to assess progress.
